title: Bay of Bengal depression set to become Cyclone Murasu, with Andhra landfall forecast for Tuesday
dek: IMD expects a cyclonic storm with gusts of up to 100 kmph to hit the Andhra Pradesh coast on 3 November, with very heavy rain from Monday. Its November outlook forecasts below-normal rain and a warm month.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
A depression has formed over the southeast Bay of Bengal and is forecast to strengthen into a cyclonic storm and hit the Andhra Pradesh coast on Tuesday morning, 3 November, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said on Saturday. If it becomes a cyclone it will be named Murasu, a name proposed by India, and will be the second cyclonic storm over the Bay this year after Arnab.

IMD Director General Mrutyunjay Mohapatra said the storm could bring winds of 80-90 kmph, gusting to 100 kmph, Business Standard reported. The IMD has forecast very heavy rain in coastal Andhra Pradesh and Rayalaseema on 2 and 3 November, with isolated extremely heavy falls, and heavy rain in southern Odisha on 3 and 4 November.

## Where the system is now

The low-pressure area over the Andaman Sea concentrated into a depression at 11.30 am IST on Saturday over the southeast Bay of Bengal and the adjoining Andaman and Nicobar Islands, DT Next reported, citing the IMD. It is expected to move west-northwest, intensify into a deep depression over the next 12 hours and into a cyclonic storm in the 12 hours after that. The IMD expects it to reach the west-central Bay of Bengal, near the Andhra Pradesh coast, by the evening of 2 November. The IMD has not yet named a landfall point.

Reports differed during the day on how quickly the system had developed: India TV, at 3.31 pm, still described it as a well-marked low expected to become a depression within six hours. Andhra Pradesh's State Disaster Management Authority said it could become a severe cyclonic storm, The Week reported.

## Rain and sea warnings

Fishermen have been told not to go to sea until at least Wednesday afternoon, and those already out have been advised to return. Mohapatra said conditions over the west-central, southeast and parts of the central Bay of Bengal would be "disastrous or devastating for any boats" from Sunday.

The Regional Meteorological Centre in Chennai has forecast heavy rain at isolated places in the Nilgiris and Tiruvallur on 2 November and in Cuddalore, Villupuram and Puducherry on 3 November. Kerala has yellow alerts in several districts between 1 and 4 November, The Week reported.

## What it means for Bengal

The IMD's Kolkata centre said in its Friday bulletin that it had issued no warning for West Bengal in connection with the system, which it is watching. It forecast light to moderate rain in Kolkata, the 24 Parganas, East Midnapore, Birbhum, Murshidabad and Nadia until Sunday morning, light rain across south Bengal until 4 November, and dry weather from 4 November. In north Bengal, Darjeeling, Jalpaiguri, Kalimpong, Alipurduar and Cooch Behar can expect light to moderate rain until Sunday, with a risk of landslides in the hills.

## A dry, warm November ahead

Separately, the IMD's monthly outlook, issued on Saturday, said November rainfall over the country as a whole and over south peninsular India is most likely to be below normal, under 77% of the long-period average. The all-India November average is about 29.7 mm, and about 118.7 mm for the south peninsula, which depends on the northeast monsoon. Some areas of central, northwest, east and Northeast India may see normal or above-normal rain.

Day temperatures are likely to be above normal over most of the country, except along the Himalayan foothills. Night temperatures are also expected to be above normal, except in many parts of central and eastern India, where they may be normal or below normal.

The IMD said "very strong El Nino conditions" are prevailing over the equatorial Pacific and are likely to persist through November and December.

## What happens next

The IMD will issue bulletins several times a day as the depression strengthens, and will name the cyclone and give a landfall point once it reaches cyclonic-storm strength. Its December forecast and winter outlook are due at the end of November.

image.alt: Day-by-day timeline of the forecast as of Saturday 31 October. Saturday: low over the Andaman Sea became a depression at 11.30 am IST. Sunday 1 November: expected to become a cyclonic storm named Murasu; fishermen told to stay ashore. Monday 2 November: system nears the Andhra coast by evening; very heavy rain in coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema. Tuesday 3 November: landfall on the Andhra Pradesh coast in the morning, winds 80-90 kmph gusting to 100 kmph; heavy rain in southern Odisha. Wednesday 4 November: heavy rain in southern Odisha; dry weather returns to south Bengal.
